correctness.rationale: The strongly regular adjacency polynomial gives the exact inverse Laplacian action on each edge dipole; the resulting five-level potential has co-ordered step decomposition. Direct cut-edge counting proves every column formula, and orthogonal-projector diagonal bounds prove the complementary formula. The 4x4 rook local graph has two triangles and the Shrikhande local graph a six-cycle, giving exact different T values. Reconstructed grounded-Laplacian inverses independently verify 333 edge columns across eight strongly regular graphs, including all 96 columns of the cospectral pair. The all-graph proof, not the enumeration, establishes the universal quantifier.

evidence: The common effective resistance R=2(m+mu)/(mu*n) fixes only Q(e,e), while the total absolute column sum also uses induced edges in U and V.
The rook and Shrikhande graphs have the same strongly regular parameters, hence the same edge effective resistance and adjacency spectrum, but their computed absolute column sums differ by 1/8.
A standard complementary-column identity P-col = Q-col+1-2R accounts for the cycle offset but does not imply either cut norm.

originality.rationale: Targeted primary full-text examination, theorem-level implication comparisons, historical claim matching and research-record searches did not locate the claimed universal exclusive-neighbor local-edge formula or its cut/cycle norm separation of the Shrikhande and 4x4 rook graphs. The general projection formalism and diagonal-resistance correction are known and excluded from the novelty claim. An equivalent but poorly indexed calculation remains a material risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed or differently named transfer-current total-variation calculations may contain an equivalent identity.

Previous results on the rook and Shrikhande graphs already distinguish them by combinatorial or topological invariants; only the projection-norm distinction and universal local formula are proposed as new.
No independent literature expert or external formal proof audit has confirmed originality.

value.rationale: The result gives an exact operator-norm classification for every connected unweighted strongly regular graph using a natural local exclusive-neighborhood edge invariant. The theorem isolates specific information absent from the spectrum and all four standard strongly regular parameters; it distinguishes the classical cospectral Shrikhande/rook pair in two natural endpoint Banach operator norms. This structural observation is not a routine tabulation or the already-known effective-resistance diagonal correction.
